Q1: L-Glutamine is largely characterized by data deficiency across most hazard classes, including carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, reproductive hazards (CMR), environmental, endocrine disruption (EDC), inhalation (IHL), dermal/eye (SKN), and organ/systemic (OGN) hazards. It shows a demonstrated low to moderate hazard for oral exposure (ORL).
Q2: L-Glutamine is not found on any lists of concern. It is listed as a "Substance added to Food" by the EPA, indicating it is generally considered of low concern for food applications.
Q3: L-Glutamine is a structurally well-defined small molecule with a substantial body of scientific literature, evidenced by 88,000 references. However, its hazard characterization is incomplete, with many hazard classes showing data deficiency, only a moderate number of specific toxicity values reported, and no formal EPA IRIS or PPRTV evaluations.
